text:
Carolina scored seven, but the more telling number is 4.70 expected goals to Vancouver's 2.68. The Hurricanes were the better team by a wide margin, deserving the win in 79 percent of simulated replays, and the 7-2 score ran well past that gap. Kevin Lankinen faced 18 shots, allowed six goals, and finished 2.85 goals worse than the chances he saw would suggest.

The first period decided the tone. CAR out-chanced VAN 1.63 to 0.49 in expected goals and led 3-0 by the 9:25 mark. K'Andre Miller opened the scoring at 1:18 with a snap shot, and Andrei Svechnikov added two power-play goals, at 7:11 and 9:25. Carolina went 3 for 3 on the man advantage while Vancouver went 0 for 4. Jake DeBrusk cut it to 4-1 early in the second, but Logan Stankoven answered with a shorthanded goal at 13:13 and a power-play goal at 19:02 to make it 6-1.

Stankoven finished with three goals on five shots and the first star. Sean Walker collected four assists, and Jackson Blake had a 25 percent chance stopped by Lankinen in the second. The late stretch was closer than the score implied, with Vancouver generating 1.13 expected goals in the third to Carolina's 1.55. DeBrusk's second goal came at 13:04 on a 54 percent look, and he finished with 1.36 expected goals of his own. Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 18 of 20 shots for CAR.
